events.title: Rudd Concession
hints: In 1888 a king granted three Europeans exclusive mining rights in return for guns and a monthly payment.
He later repudiated the document, saying he had been misled about what it said.
Cecil Rhodes used it to get a royal charter for his company.
events.summary: In October 1888 King Lobengula of the Ndebele signed the Rudd Concession, granting exclusive mining rights in return for rifles and a monthly sum. He later disputed what it meant, but Cecil Rhodes used it to obtain a royal charter for the British South Africa Company in 1889.

events.title: Pioneer Column and the Matabele wars
hints: A column of settlers escorted by armed police crossed into Mashonaland in 1890.
Maxim guns defeated Ndebele forces in 1893 and again in 1896.
Rebellions by the Ndebele and Shona in 1896-97 were crushed and cattle and land were seized.
events.summary: In 1890 the Pioneer Column occupied Mashonaland on behalf of Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company. The company defeated the Ndebele in 1893, and the Ndebele and Shona risings of 1896-1897 were crushed, with cattle and land confiscated.

events.title: Land Apportionment Act
hints: A 1930 law divided the land into areas for European and African ownership.
Europeans, a small fraction of the population, received the larger and better share.
Tobacco farming on the reserved land became the backbone of the economy.
events.summary: The 1930 Land Apportionment Act divided Southern Rhodesia into European and African areas, reserving the best land for the white minority. It forced many Africans into overcrowded reserves and underpinned a tobacco-based settler economy until it was replaced by the Land Tenure Act in 1969.

events.title: Unilateral Declaration of Independence and the Bush War
hints: In November 1965 a white-minority government declared independence from Britain.
United Nations sanctions followed, but some partners kept trading with the regime.
A guerrilla war ended with the Lancaster House talks in 1979.
events.summary: In November 1965 Ian Smith's Rhodesian Front declared independence to preserve white-minority rule. UN sanctions followed, and a guerrilla war against the regime lasted until the 1979 Lancaster House Agreement led to majority rule.

events.title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
territoryNames: the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
hints: Britain linked three territories under a federal government in 1953.
The settler-dominated south held the capital and most of the benefits.
African nationalists opposed it, and it broke up in 1963.
events.summary: The Central African Federation, created in 1953 by Britain, tied together Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland. The settler-dominated south held the capital and gained most of the benefits, and African nationalists opposed it until it dissolved in 1963.
